solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ancient and backward Russian area: no good

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the Russian and the area from right to left

blocks.note: Oleg is a typical Russian man's name
A is the abbreviation for area
NG is the usual shorthand for no good

explanation.surface: A description of some ancient, underdeveloped and worthless stretch of Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the Russian and the area are turned round; the no-good abbreviation is added afterwards, unreversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Agelong means lasting for ages, so something agelong is very old, i.e. of great antiquity.

clue.text: Mistress maybe rather like a team member

blocks.note: rather, as in somewhat, is a bit
a team member is on the side

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a mistress is a bit like a member of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' warns that a mistress is only one example of what the phrase can describe: a secret lover of either sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit on the side is informal British slang for a lover taken outside a marriage or relationship, of which a mistress is an example.

clue.text: Without echo, pleasing effect

blocks.note: ex is Latin for without, as in ex dividend
Echo is the NATO alphabet word for E
something cute is pleasing to look at

explanation.surface: Something has a pleasing effect even without any echo, perhaps in a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Effect' looks like a noun but is the verb, meaning bring about.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect a plan is to carry it out, and to execute a plan is likewise to carry it out.

clue.text: Bloomer concealed by cagey ex-officer on the way up

indicators.note: concealed by says the word sits inside the letters of the following phrase
in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of cagey and the start of ex-officer, read backwards

explanation.surface: A blunder is covered up by a secretive former officer who is rising in rank.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is usually a blunder, but here it is literally something that blooms: a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxeye daisy is a common flowering plant, so it is a bloomer in the crossword sense of a flower.

clue.text: One sponsored or in receipt of Washington greeting

indicators.note: something in receipt of other letters has taken them in, so they go inside it

blocks.note: or is the heraldic word for gold, which is the outer piece
Washington DC, the US capital
a common greeting

explanation.surface: Someone is either sponsored or else has received a welcome from Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' is not a conjunction: in heraldry or means gold, and the word GOLD wraps around the capital and the greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: At a christening godparents act as sponsors, vouching for the baptised child, who is their godchild.

clue.text: Two shakes and something to eat with it

blocks.note: two shakes (of a lamb's tail) means a moment, shortened to mo
a dish is a prepared item of food

explanation.surface: A recipe: a couple of shakes and some food to have alongside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something to eat with' looks like cutlery, but the definition is the slang phrase with it, meaning trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with it is fashionable and up to date, which is what modish means.

clue.text: Miss having drive in European city

indicators.note: the girl is having, i.e. holding, the other letters within her

blocks.note: a maid is an unmarried girl, a miss
Dr is the street-name abbreviation for Drive

explanation.surface: A young woman with a car journey in some city of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Madrid is the capital of Spain, and so a city in Europe.

clue.text: Bold attorney coming down on extreme left-wing immorality

blocks.note: a DA is a district attorney in the US
a red is a communist, at the far left of politics
evil is wickedness, immorality

explanation.surface: A brave lawyer cracks down on the immoral behaviour of the radical left.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'coming down on' places the attorney above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Daredevil works as an adjective for recklessly brave behaviour, close to bold in sense.

clue.text: Celebrated editor's being replaced

indicators.note: being replaced suggests the letters are moved out of their places and set down differently

blocks.note: taken letter for letter, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: News that a famous editor is being sacked and replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Storied means famous in story or legend, so a storied career is a celebrated one.

clue.text: One's staggered and dived in recklessly, without hesitation

indicators.note: doing something recklessly means without care for order, so the letters are thrown about
without is used in its old sense of outside, so the scrambled letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: the words taken as written, for shuffling
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A diver lurches and plunges in carelessly, without a moment's pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without hesitation' reads as straight away, but without means outside: the shuffled letters go round the hesitation sound.
explanation.definitionFit: I never did is an exclamation of astonishment, said by someone who is amazed.

clue.text: Resting place with a sense of belonging: time to go back

indicators.note: to go back means one letter leaves its place and moves to the rear

blocks.note: your roots give you a feeling of where you belong
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A home where one feels one belongs, and it is time to return there.
explanation.walkthrough: The time letter in the belonging word is taken from its place and put back at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is where birds settle to rest or sleep, hence a resting place.

clue.text: Right to enter you once controlled — so old hat?

indicators.note: to enter means to go into the word that follows

blocks.note: thee is the archaic form of you
R is the abbreviation for right
to corner a market is to control it

explanation.surface: A rightful claim to something you used to own — is that now passé?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like a phrase meaning outdated, but it is a literal old hat: the tricorne. Its shape is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The tricorne, worn in the eighteenth century, is a hat with three corners, so such a hat is three-cornered.

clue.text: Cipher to become one that's serviceable

blocks.note: a cipher is a zero, written as O
things that fuse merge into a single whole

explanation.surface: Instructions for a code to merge into something usable.
explanation.walkthrough: A cipher here is nought, not a code.
explanation.definitionFit: Something serviceable is usable and functional, which is to say helpful or of use.

clue.text: Husband getting Scottish town councillor, finally, on the blower

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
Airdrie is a town near Glasgow
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A husband phones to say he has been landed with a councillor from a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the blower' is British slang for on the telephone, but here the blower is a device that blows hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdrier blows warm air to dry hair, so it is literally a blower.

clue.text: Area of SE Europe has flourished with style

indicators.note: flourished suggests letters being waved about with a flourish, so they come down in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A region of south-eastern Europe has thrived with elegance.
explanation.definitionFit: Thessaly is a historic region of central Greece, so it lies in south-east Europe.

clue.text: Ashes partner's dismissal, caught, showing hesitancy

blocks.note: getting the sack is being dismissed from a job
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
loth means reluctant, hesitant

explanation.surface: A cricket report: in the Ashes, a batting partner is dismissed, caught after a hesitant shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes are the England–Australia cricket series, but here they are the ashes of the phrase sackcloth and ashes, worn in mourning or penitence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sackcloth is traditionally paired with ashes in the idiom for public penitence, so it is the ashes' partner.

clue.text: Name miss deliberately has adopted?

indicators.note: something that has adopted another takes it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to evade is to avoid on purpose
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A question about the name that a girl has chosen to take on.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: Evadne is the name you get when the dodging word takes in the name letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Evadne is a female first name from Greek mythology, borne by the wife of Capaneus.

clue.text: Get round pear used for cooking

indicators.note: something for cooking will be chopped and mixed, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kitchen note: a round pear is the one used for cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get round' looks like an instruction about the fruit's shape; it means win someone over.
explanation.definitionFit: To get round someone is to coax them into agreeing, which is to convince or win them over.

clue.text: Take out pills to have inside eatery on return

indicators.note: the first piece is to have the next inside it, holding it within
on return means the whole result is then read backwards

blocks.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so pills are two of them
a caff is British slang for a cheap cafe

explanation.surface: Someone takes out some tablets to swallow on getting back to a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The pills are a pair of ecstasy tablets, one at each end of the cheap eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface something is to rub it out or erase it, removing it from view.

clue.text: Some film for which you need to pay on time

blocks.note: to foot a bill is to pay it
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A cinema-goer is told a film must be paid for punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the payment above the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Footage is recorded film material, so some footage is a length of film.

clue.text: Comfortable space in one's in-tray?

blocks.note: a well is an open space, as in a stairwell
what sits in an in-tray is work still to do

explanation.surface: An office worker happy to have room to spare in the in-tray.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose sense: an in-tray holds the jobs that are still to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfortable can mean financially secure, and the well-to-do are prosperous people.

clue.text: Eight clubs support, of course, holding races with preliminary round

indicators.note: holding means the support wraps around the races
preliminary says the round comes first, at the front of everything

blocks.note: a round shape is an O
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a tee supports the ball on a golf course
the TT races are the Isle of Man motorcycle races

explanation.surface: A golf club's eight-man team supports, of course, a run of races with a first round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' is not a shrug: it means on a golf course, where a tee holds up the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: An octette is a group of eight, such as eight musicians, so it means eight.

clue.text: Did Harry and his best friend, say, upset daughter?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from the bottom up

blocks.note: the dog is man's best friend
eg, for example, is what say means here
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A question whether Prince Harry and his closest friend annoyed a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a name, but here it is a verb, to harass; his best friend is man's best friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow and harass them persistently, so dogged is the past tense of harry.

clue.text: Press put out award in Germany once

blocks.note: to press clothes is to iron them
someone put out is annoyed, cross

explanation.surface: The newspapers were displeased by a historic German honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the newspapers but is the household chore.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross was a Prussian and later German military decoration for bravery, no longer awarded.

clue.text: Mattress that's folded or closed in amusement?

indicators.note: in places the closed word inside the amusement

blocks.note: fun is amusement
a door pulled to is closed

explanation.surface: A mattress that is either folded away or shut inside some fairground ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folded' describes the definition: a futon folds up into a sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a thin Japanese-style mattress, often folded up when not used for sleeping.

clue.text: Shy Yankee leaving in a plane, possibly

indicators.note: leaving means that letter departs from the longer word

blocks.note: Yankee is the NATO alphabet word for Y
in a plane is one way of flying, hence possibly

explanation.surface: A timid American leaves on a flight, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' reads as timid but is a verb, to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy a ball, as at a coconut shy, is to throw it, and a fling is likewise a throw.

clue.text: Deserter in east: old one behind the lines?

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for east
a rat deserts a sinking ship
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A soldier who deserted on the eastern front, an old man who stayed behind enemy lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The lines are not military front lines but lines of verse: the muse inspires them.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek muse of lyric and love poetry, so she is the inspiration behind lines of verse.

clue.text: Go off to help a large retreating combatant

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so everything before it is read right to left

blocks.note: food that goes off rots
aid is help
taken as written
LG is an abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An order to leave and assist a big fighter who is withdrawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator was a trained fighter who fought in the Roman arena, so a combatant.

clue.text: Approach police leading stretcher-bearer?

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
a stretcher is a brick laid lengthwise, and a hod carries bricks

explanation.surface: The police arrive at the scene, followed by someone carrying a stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: The stretcher-bearer is not a medic: in bricklaying a stretcher is a brick laid along the wall, and a hod carries bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: An approach to a problem is a way of tackling it, which is a method.

clue.text: Intellectual urge by bloke to get promotion

blocks.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
a bloke is a man, he
an ad promotes a product

explanation.surface: A clever person pushes a man to seek a step up at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' suggests a step up at work, but here it is advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is an informal word for a highly academic, bookish person, an intellectual.
